Okay, the user still can't see the UI changes—they posted a screenshot indicating the UI hasn't updated. I've already built the UI locally (`pnpm build`) and copied the freshly built `ui/dist` into the server's UI distribution directory (`@paperclipai/server/ui-dist`). The copy succeeded, and I listed the assets in the target directory, confirming that the new bundle files (e.g., `apl-B4CMkyY2.js`, `architectureDiagram-VXUJARFQ-2nzfEgzH.js`, etc.) are present alongside the `index.html`. 

Now I need to verify that the running server (listening on port 3100) is actually serving the newly copied bundle, not still serving the old one from the previous installation. The simplest way is to request the `/GLI/issues` endpoint, which returns the main HTML page that references the UI bundle via a `<script src="/assets/index-XXXX.js">`. If the server has reloaded the static files, the `src` attribute should point to a new filename (the hash part will have changed). 

So I will:
1. Curl the page and extract the `src="/assets/index-...` string to see which bundle filename is being referenced now.
2. Capture that filename (or at least the first matching one) into a variable `NEWJS`.
3. Echo the bundle name for debugging.
4. Fetch that JS file directly from the server (`http://127.0.0.1:3100$NEWJS`) and search for a known marker that should appear only in the newly built UI. In the recent UI changes we added a “Clear & cancel all” button, which is rendered by the new bundle. Therefore I can count occurrences of the string `"Clear & cancel all"` in the JS file; a non‑zero count would confirm the new bundle is being served.

All of this can be done in a single Bash command, chaining the curls and greps, and storing the intermediate filename in `NEWJS`. This will give me a clear verification step before I tell the user the UI should now be updated, or before I consider further troubleshooting if the old bundle is still being served.

Thus I will run the composed curl/grep command as a tool call.ASSISTANT (tool call) Bash input={"command": "curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3100/GLI/issues | grep -o 'src=\"/assets/index-[^\"]*\"'; NEWJS=$(curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3100/GLI/issues | grep -o '/assets/index-[^\"]*\\.js' | head -1); echo \"bundle: $NEWJS\"; curl -s \"http://127.0.0.1:3100$NEWJS\" | grep -c \"Clear & cancel all\"", "description": "Verify server serves new bundle with button"}
